COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
18.09.2024 SPA No. 221 of 2024
Hon'ble Ritu Bahri, C.J. 
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg and Mr. Pankaj Tangwan, 
learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. K.N. Joshi, 
learned Deputy Advocate General for the State / 
respondent Nos. 1 to 3, Mr. Naresh Pant, learned 
counsel for respondent No. 4 and Mr. Tapan Singh, 
learned counsel for respondent No. 5. 
2. After hearing the learned counsel for the 
parties, the short question for consideration in the 
present Appeal is, whether out of the 
compensation taken by the appellant, the 
respondent has the share of 1/4th. It is not in 
dispute that the partition proceedings are going on 
before the Assistant Collector, First Class, Haridwar 
as Case No. 5 of 2018 under Section 176 of the 
Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land 
Reforms Act. 
3. As per the observation made in Paragraph-8
of the impugned order passed by the learned Single 
Judge dated 25.06.2024, respondent No. 5 was 
claiming 1/4th share in the land comprising in 
Khasra No. 280.  4. Since respondent No. 5 is claiming 1/4th
share, the order dated 25th June, 2024 is being
modified that the appellant-writ petitioner will 
deposit only 1/4th compensation received by him on 
11.11.2021 and pursuant to the order dated 
25.06.2024, he has deposited the entire 
compensation before the Special Land Acquisition 
Officer, Haridwar. 
5. Keeping in view that the respondent No. 5 
has only deposited 1/4th amount, the order dated 
25th June, 2024 is being modified that the 
competent Authority, where the compensation was 
deposited by the appellant-writ petitioner, will 
retain 1/4th share of the amount and will release 
rest of the amount to the present appellant. 
6. The present Appeal is admitted to be listed 
for hearing after the partition suit is decided. 
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J) (Ritu Bahri, CJ) 
 18.09.2024 18.09.2024 
Rathour

orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. G. NARENDAR
AND 
HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
25TH APRIL, 2025
SPECIAL APPEAL NO.221 OF 2024
Rajveer Singh …...Appellant
Versus
District Magistrate and Others …….Respondents
Counsel for the appellant : Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate.
Counsel for the respondent : Mr. Yogesh Tiwari, Addl. 
Nos.1 to 3 C.S.C.
Counsel for the respondent : Mr. Naresh Pant, Advocate
No.4. (through video conferencing)
Counsel for the respondent : Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate 
No.5 
ORDER :(per Mr. G. Narendar, C.J.)
The matter was admitted on 18.09.2024. 
2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that on 
filing of the suit for partition, being Suit No.5 of 2018, the 
court had issued notices and the parties have put in 
appearance and have filed their respective statements and, 
thereafter, nothing much has progressed. The pendency of 
a suit for partition, for nearly 07 years is in the teeth of
1 Rule 3 of the Uttarakhand Case Flow Management (For 
Subordinate Courts) Rules, 2009, which clearly stipulate 
that suits of such nature are required to be heard and 
disposed of within two years from the date of appearance 
or deemed appearance of defendant-respondent-opposite 
party. The relevant rule reads as under :-
“3. Categorisation of suits/ Cases/ Appeals/
Revisions and other proceedings into Tracks-
(1) The Presiding Officer of the court shall categories 
the suits/cases and proceedings in his Court into track￾I, Track-II and Track-III based on the nature of 
dispute, the quantum of evidence to be recorded and 
the time likely to be taken for the completion of trial of 
the suit, the suits shall be channeled into different 
tracks.
(i) Track-I : Cases relating to (1) matrimonial 
matters (2) maintenance (3) custody of children 
(4) appointment of guardian and wards (5) 
visitation rights (6) grant of letters of 
administration (7) succession certificate (8) Small 
Causes Suits (9) Rent Control Appeals (10) 
revisions (11) miscellaneous cases (12) election 
petitions (13) Motor Accident Claims Petitions 
(14) money suits based solely on 
promotes/negotiable instruments (15) execution 
cases (16) miscellaneous appeals. 
(ii) Track-II : (1) Original suits (other than 
mentioned in track-I) (2) Suits for trademarks, 
copyrights, patents and intellectual property 
rights (3) Land Acquisition References. 
(iii) Track-III : Such other cases not included in 
Track-I to II shall be posted in Track-III. 
(2) The Presiding Officer shall endeavor to dispose of 
cases in Track-I within one year and the cases in tack￾II & III within two years from the date of appearance 
or deemed appearance of defendant-respondent￾opposite party. 
Note- For the period court remained vacant or 
proceeding remained stayed under the orders of 
superior court shall not be taken into account for 
calculating maximum period.
2 (i) Where statute requires that suits/proceedings 
have to be completed within a specified period then 
the above mentioned period for deciding the suits shall 
not apply, and the Court shall decide the suit with in 
the given statutory period. Time limit fixed for various 
stages of civil suits as per Code of Civil Procedure shall 
be adhered to
(ii) …
(3) …
(4) …
(5) …
(6) …
(7) …”
3. In that view, we direct the Court of Assistant 
Collector, Ist Class, Haridwar to hear and dispose of Suit 
No. 5 of 2018 titled as ‘Biram Singh and Another vs. 
Rajveer and Others’ pending on his file, as expeditiously as 
possible but at any rate within an outer limit of four months 
from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
4. The parties shall appear before the Court of 
Assistant Collector, Ist Class, Haridwar on 05.05.2025 at 
03:00 P.M. and shall not be permitted any adjournment 
except in the case of any grave situation or serious health 
crisis leading to hospitalization. We would request the 
court of Assistant Collector, Ist Class, Haridwar to attempt 
to hear and dispose of the suit on day to day basis. 
5. List immediately after four months. 
6. The concerned court is directed to inform this 
Court about the disposal of the said suit before the next 
date fixed. 
3 7. The Registry is directed to forthwith forward a 
certified copy of this to the concerned court by way of e￾mail. 
________________
G. NARENDAR, C.J.
 __________________
ALOK KUMR VERMA, J.
Dt: 25thApril, 2025
